title: Choose a Deployment Shape and Operating Model
summary: Choose among workstation, container, on-premises, edge, cloud, and hybrid shapes from workload evidence, data boundaries, ownership, recovery needs, and reversible operating decisions.
objectives: Translate a model-serving idea into a bounded workload, service objective, data boundary, and failure budget.
Compare workstation, container, on-premises, edge, and cloud deployment shapes without assuming one is inherently private, cheap, or reliable.
Assign identity, security, platform, model, data, evaluation, capacity, incident, and recovery ownership.
Select a reversible initial shape with explicit evidence, constraints, review triggers, and an exit path.

sections.title: Define the workload before choosing a platform
paragraphs: Instructor narration: begin with the service contract because a platform is only suitable relative to a workload and its failure consequences. Record the users, tasks, model class, input and output modalities, sensitivity, concurrency, arrival pattern, context size, output length, latency objective, availability target, geographic boundary, disconnected requirement, retention rule, and recovery objective. Separate an experiment, a shared internal service, and a production dependency because they justify different operating commitments.

Record what happens when the endpoint is slow, unavailable, overloaded, wrong, unsafe, or unable to process a request. A deployment shape is suitable only when the team can operate both its normal path and its failure path. A retry response, safe refusal, traffic stop, or human queue can be an intentional failure response. Silent loss or an undocumented bypass cannot.

Worked workload dated 2026-09-21: a synthetic internal support assistant serves 120 analysts in one country. It receives 60 requests per minute at the 95th-percentile demand point and bursts to 120 requests per minute. Inputs contain 2,000 to 8,000 tokens and outputs are capped at 800 tokens. The model class is a text-generating language model accessed through an internal text-in and text-out service. The data is confidential internal text and must remain in-country. No disconnected operation is required.

The synthetic service objectives are p95 latency of 4 seconds or less, 99.5 percent monthly availability, recovery time objective, or RTO, of 60 minutes, and recovery point objective, or RPO, of 15 minutes. Inputs are retained for 7 days for approved evaluation and then deleted. Audit events are retained for 90 days. When the service is unavailable, requests enter an approved human queue. When overloaded, the service returns a retryable response rather than dropping work. Unsafe or unprocessable requests stop safely and are routed for human review.

These figures define the exercise and are not measurements of any model, accelerator, runtime, API, provider, or deployment. A real team would establish capacity and latency with representative prompts, the exact model artifact, the exact serving runtime, target hardware, and controlled load tests. The lab fixtures contain decision evidence only. They do not execute a model or establish that any service objective has been achieved.
sections.callout: Start with the service contract and failure consequences, not the hardware catalog.

sections.title: Compare five useful deployment shapes
paragraphs: Instructor narration: a deployment label describes part of a topology, not a completed control system. A workstation can support individual learning, offline experiments, and low-concurrency development, but user sessions, sleep, local privilege, thermal limits, and unmanaged changes make it a weak default for a shared service. A container adds a reproducible process boundary and packaging contract. It does not by itself add strong isolation, authentication, backups, high availability, or resource limits.

On-premises infrastructure can align with local data, connectivity, and hardware-control requirements while transferring capacity, patching, power, cooling, spare-parts, and incident ownership to the operator. Edge deployments reduce distance or support intermittent connectivity but constrain power, memory, update bandwidth, physical security, and repair.

Cloud compute can provide faster provisioning, managed infrastructure options, and elastic capacity, but it still requires verified region, identity, networking, encryption, quotas, cost controls, observability, backup, and exit planning. Hybrid designs add routing, consistency, identity, and operational choices. None of these labels proves privacy, cost efficiency, performance, or resilience.

Use hard constraints before weighted ranking. For this packet, the mandatory constraints are evidence that the selected option matches the required data boundary, has RTO no worse than 60 minutes, has RPO no worse than 15 minutes, and has a qualified owner for the bounded evaluation. Unknown evidence is accepted as an incomplete input state, but it does not satisfy a constraint. Negative recovery values, unsupported enum values, non-finite numbers, missing alternatives, and duplicate alternatives are malformed inputs rather than incomplete evidence.

After eligibility, every option uses the same illustrative weights: capacity and latency fit 25 points, scalability 20, operability 20, reversibility 15, cost predictability 10, and workload fit 10. The arithmetic is: workstation 4 + 2 + 2 + 5 + 3 + 2 = 18; containerized single host 15 + 10 + 10 + 14 + 8 + 7 = 64; on-premises service 20 + 14 + 17 + 12 + 8 + 7 = 78; edge appliance 10 + 5 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 55; cloud service 25 + 20 + 18 + 15 + 9 + 5 = 92; hybrid 19 + 17 + 14 + 10 + 8 + 5 = 73. These are synthetic decision scores, not benchmark results.

The comparable evidence matrix is as follows. Workstation: boundary unknown, RTO 1,440 minutes, RPO 1,440 minutes, owner missing, score 18, ineligible. Containerized single host: local-only boundary verified, RTO 180, RPO 60, owner qualified, score 64, ineligible on recovery. On-premises service: local-only boundary verified, RTO 60, RPO 15, owner qualified for the evaluation, score 78, eligible. Edge appliance: local-only boundary verified, RTO 120, RPO 60, owner qualified, score 55, ineligible on recovery. Cloud service: boundary unknown, recovery unknown, owner missing, score 92, ineligible despite the highest score. Hybrid: local-only boundary verified, RTO 60, RPO 15, owner qualified, score 73, eligible but lower-ranked.

A container has no resource constraints by default, so CPU and memory limits and host-capacity evidence must be configured and verified rather than inferred from packaging. Docker documents this behavior at https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/resource_constraints/. Kubernetes resource settings and security guidance likewise describe configuration mechanisms and checks, not proof that a particular deployment enforces them: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ and https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/security-checklist/.

Keep model family, artifact, runtime, hardware integration, and API as separate decision fields. Meta Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Microsoft Phi, and NVIDIA model or runtime offerings may be evaluated when their specific licenses, artifacts, supported runtimes, hardware targets, and interfaces fit the workload. Their names do not establish equivalent APIs, quality, security controls, licenses, context limits, or operating contracts. ONNX Runtime execution providers illustrate a runtime-to-hardware integration boundary, including provider-specific execution paths, but do not prove that every model family supports every provider: https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/execution-providers/.

Real integration requires testing the exact selected artifact and version, runtime and version, host or accelerator, resource limits, identity path, network policy, storage path, registry, telemetry, backup, and restore procedure. The supplied lab is deliberately narrower. It simulates previously collected evidence and repairs decision ordering. It makes no live API call and cannot approve a model, provider, or production deployment.
sections.callout: A workstation, container, edge, cloud, or hybrid label never establishes privacy, cost, performance, or availability.

sections.title: Separate process, host, site, and control-plane failure domains
paragraphs: Instructor narration: redundancy only helps when replicas do not share the failure being tested. List the process, container, device, host, accelerator, storage, network, identity provider, scheduler, site, region, registry, and management-plane dependencies. For each dependency, decide whether the response is to restart the process, replace a replica, move to another node, fail over to another site, shed load, or stop safely.

Do not claim high availability because multiple replicas exist on one host or because an orchestrator can restart a broken process. Test the actual failure domain and confirm that state, secrets, model artifacts, queues, and routing remain recoverable.

Filled failure-domain map for the support assistant: a process crash triggers a bounded restart; a container failure replaces the replica; an image defect rolls back to the prior approved digest; an accelerator failure moves service to a tested spare host; a host failure moves traffic to another host; storage corruption invokes a restore test against the RPO; network loss sheds traffic to the human queue; and site loss invokes the approved secondary-site procedure. A region failure matters only if the chosen topology uses a cloud region.

Shared dependencies remain after replica placement. Identity-provider loss stops new requests safely because there is no emergency authentication bypass. Registry loss permits use of a locally cached approved artifact but blocks new deployment. Scheduler or management-plane loss freezes changes and retains the last known-good data plane where safe. A shared site can remove every host in that site. Shared secrets, queues, storage, DNS, routing, identity, registry, or management services can also defeat apparently independent replicas.

Recovery evidence must include more than a successful process restart. The test packet must show whether the model artifact can be retrieved or safely cached, whether secrets remain available, whether queued work is preserved within the RPO, whether routing can move, and whether operators can restore the last approved configuration. A claimed RTO or RPO without a dated exercise remains unknown.

The lab fixture does not perform these failure tests. It represents outcomes such as an RTO number, an RPO number, or explicit unknown evidence. A live integration would inject controlled failures into authorized test infrastructure and collect timestamps, logs, restore checks, and routing observations.
sections.callout: Redundancy inside one shared failure domain is not evidence of availability outside that domain.

sections.title: Assign operating ownership before deployment
paragraphs: Instructor narration: assign operating work before the endpoint becomes important. Name accountable owners for model and license review, artifact integrity, host and accelerator lifecycle, runtime, identity and access, secrets, network policy, data handling, evaluation, capacity, cost, telemetry, vulnerability response, abuse handling, incident command, backup, restore, rollback, and end-of-life.

For each role, record decision authority, on-call expectation, evidence produced, escalation path, and substitute. A team name without authority, evidence, availability, escalation, and backup coverage is not a complete assignment.

Filled ownership packet for the bounded evaluation: the model steward approves the model and license and records the review; the artifact custodian verifies hashes and provenance; platform operations owns hosts, accelerators, runtime, capacity, cost, telemetry, backup, restore, rollback, and end-of-life; security owns identity, secrets, network policy, vulnerability response, and abuse handling; data governance owns classification, retention, deletion evidence, and geographic handling; evaluation owns quality and safety gates; and the incident commander coordinates incidents and declares recovery.

Each accepted evaluation assignment records decision authority, a business-hours response expectation, its evidence location, escalation to the service owner, and a named substitute where available. The selector's `requiredOwner` field compresses this packet into a fixture enum. `qualified` means the bounded evaluation has accepted coverage. It does not mean every future production responsibility is permanently staffed.

Two production gaps remain unresolved: there is no qualified substitute for the artifact custodian, and no owner has accepted after-hours incident command. Therefore the decision authorizes only a staffed business-hours evaluation. It does not authorize a 24-hour production dependency. If the evaluation itself loses qualified coverage, every option becomes ineligible until coverage is restored or the workload is reduced to a safely bounded experiment.
sections.callout: Useful ownership includes authority, evidence, escalation, on-call expectation, and a substitute.

sections.title: Choose the smallest reversible shape that proves the next claim
paragraphs: Instructor narration: select the smallest shape that can safely answer the next decision, such as whether the exact artifact and runtime work, whether representative quality passes, whether one host meets capacity, or whether a shared service meets reliability. Avoid building multi-site orchestration before a bounded endpoint contract has been evaluated.

Apply the hard constraints before ranking. Workstation, containerized single host, edge appliance, and cloud service are rejected because one or more mandatory constraints are unmet or unknown. On-premises service and hybrid are eligible. Their scores are 78 and 73, so on-premises service is selected. If eligible options tie, sort their documented option IDs in ascending lexicographic order. A high score never overrides an unmet data-boundary, recovery, or owner constraint.

Rejected alternatives remain useful evidence. Workstation is rejected for shared-service operation and recovery. Containerized single host is rejected because packaging does not remove the host failure domain and its 180-minute RTO and 60-minute RPO miss the objectives. Edge is rejected because its 120-minute RTO and 60-minute RPO miss the objectives, while disconnected operation is not required. Cloud is rejected despite score 92 because boundary, recovery, and owner evidence are unknown or missing. Hybrid is eligible but rejected for the first evaluation because its score is lower and its routing and consistency responsibilities are not needed to prove the next claim.

The reversible decision is a staffed on-premises evaluation, not a production availability claim. The safe return state is the last approved model digest, image digest, configuration, and routing rule, with new model traffic disabled and the human queue enabled. Preserve the prior artifact and configuration until rollback has been tested. Record capacity and cost as UNKNOWN until representative load and financial measurements are collected.

Stop immediately if data-boundary evidence expires, an RTO or RPO exercise fails, qualified evaluation ownership disappears, a quality or safety gate fails, an unapproved artifact is detected, retention or deletion controls fail, or a severe incident requires containment. Migrate or redesign when host or site loss cannot meet the objective, demand exceeds the tested envelope for two review periods, the 99.5 percent objective is missed, the geography changes, or production after-hours coverage becomes required.

Review weekly during the evaluation and at least every 60 days afterward. Review sooner after a change to workload, data class, users, geography, model, artifact, runtime, demand, service objective, incident history, identity path, registry, management plane, or ownership. The exit plan is to disable routing, preserve required audit evidence, remove retained inputs according to policy, revoke service credentials, archive the decision record, and return work to the human queue.

Independent learner variation: predict before inspecting the answer. Suppose the required boundary changes to `cloud-region-verified`, cloud evidence becomes `cloud-region-verified`, cloud recovery becomes RTO 60 and RPO 15, its owner becomes qualified, and hybrid also has verified cloud-region evidence. Which option should win? Answer: cloud wins because cloud and hybrid are now eligible and their scores are 92 and 73. The cause is changed constraint evidence followed by ranking, not a hardcoded preference for cloud. Local-only options no longer match the changed boundary.
sections.callout: Choose a reversible first shape, not the most attractive shape.

sections.title: Repair the constraint-first selector
paragraphs: Instructor narration: the runnable lab isolates one defect without replacing the operating packet. The starter validates a complete six-option fixture, sorts every option by weighted score, and only then reports whether the winner is eligible. This allows the attractive but ineligible cloud option to appear first. Your repair must filter by mandatory data-boundary, recovery, and owner evidence before ranking.

The lab uses Node 22 native ECMAScript modules, built-in modules only, deterministic local JSON, no dependencies, no API keys, and no network. `validation.mjs` is shared by the learner selector and the independent reference. It accepts `null` recovery values as explicit unknown evidence but rejects negative, non-finite, and incorrectly typed values. It also requires the exact six unique option IDs and validates `requiredOwner`. Only `selector.mjs` is the learner edit.

From the repository root, run:

Before repair, the CLI stdout is exactly `{"selected":"cloud-service","eligible":false,"reason":"mandatory-constraints-not-met"}` with exit code 0. The tests print exactly `FAIL 19/27 failed=base-selection,reference-base,unknown-boundary-fallback,tie-policy,unknown-recovery-fallback,zero-eligible,cli-root,cli-lab` with exit code 1.

After repair, the same CLI command prints exactly `{"selected":"on-premises-service","eligible":true,"reason":"eligible"}` with exit code 0. The tests print exactly `PASS 27/27` with exit code 0. Run the changed input from the repository root with:

Its repaired stdout is exactly `{"selected":"cloud-service","eligible":true,"reason":"eligible"}` with exit code 0.

Prediction before answer: in the baseline, cloud has score 92 but unknown boundary and recovery evidence and a missing owner. On-premises and hybrid are eligible, with scores 78 and 73. Predict that on-premises wins. In the changed input, predict that cloud wins because the required boundary and cloud evidence change together, recovery and ownership become complete, and cloud then outranks the other eligible option.

Explained answer key: preserve the shared validator and score calculation. In `select`, call `validateDecision`, filter options with the clearly named mandatory-constraint predicate, throw `no eligible option` when the filtered array is empty, then sort only the eligible options by descending calculated score and ascending ID. Return the first eligible option. Do not weaken validation, return a canned result, deny every option, inspect the fixture filename, or hardcode an ID. Those approaches fail the changed input, fallback, tie, malformed-input, or zero-eligible tests.

Causal feedback: `base-selection` means ranking occurred before eligibility or an eligibility condition is wrong. `unknown-boundary-fallback` means unknown boundary evidence was incorrectly treated as met. `unknown-recovery-fallback` means a null recovery value was incorrectly treated as sufficient evidence. `tie-policy` means sorting did not apply ascending option ID after equal scores. `zero-eligible` means the selector returned an ineligible option instead of stopping. `cli-root` or `cli-lab` means the selector or path behavior differs by working directory.

Recovery: from the repository root run `cp training/self-hosted-model-operations/deployment-shape-and-operating-model/lab/starter.mjs training/self-hosted-model-operations/deployment-shape-and-operating-model/lab/selector.mjs`. From the lab directory run `cp starter.mjs selector.mjs`. These commands restore only the deliberately defective learner file. The tests use no operating-system temporary directory and write no files.

Rubric: a complete repair earns credit only when all 27 immutable checks pass, the baseline selects on-premises, the changed input selects cloud, unknown evidence is disqualifying rather than malformed, malformed types and ranges are rejected, zero eligible options stops with an error, and tie ordering is deterministic. Passing the code lab does not prove deployment approval. The learner must also submit the workload contract, six-shape matrix, failure-domain map, ownership packet with gaps, reversible decision, rejected alternatives, stop and migration triggers, and safe-state recovery plan.
sections.callout: Filter on mandatory evidence first, then rank eligible options.

activity.title: Create a deployment-shape decision record
instructions: Define one synthetic workload with users, data class, request distribution, context and output sizes, latency and availability objectives, disconnected needs, and recovery objectives.
Score workstation, containerized single host, on-premises service, edge appliance, cloud service, and one hybrid option against the same criteria.
Draw the process, host, site, identity, network, storage, registry, and management-plane failure domains.
Assign all operating roles and identify every role without a qualified owner.
Choose a bounded first shape, define stop and migration triggers, and write how to return to a known safe state.
Predict the baseline and changed-input winners, repair only `lab/selector.mjs`, run the Node 22 CLI and immutable tests, and explain why eligibility must precede ranking.
evidence: A dated workload and service contract with normal and failure behavior.
A comparable shape matrix, failure-domain map, and ownership matrix.
A reversible decision record with rejected alternatives, stop conditions, migration path, and review triggers.
A repaired selector that produces the documented stdout, passes all 27 tests, and handles the independent changed input without hardcoded IDs.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which attractive platform feature does not address your workload's most consequential failure?

questions.prompt: What should be defined before choosing hardware or cloud services?
choices: Users, workload, data, demand, service objectives, failures, and recovery
questions.explanation: The service and failure contract determines what infrastructure evidence is relevant.

questions.prompt: What does putting a model server in a container establish by itself?
choices: Reproducible packaging and a process boundary, subject to the actual configuration
questions.explanation: Containers help package and bound processes but do not automatically provide the other controls.

questions.prompt: Why are two replicas on one host insufficient evidence for host availability?
choices: Both replicas share the same host failure domain
questions.explanation: Redundancy inside a shared failure domain does not survive loss of that domain.

questions.prompt: Which statement about local deployment is accurate?
choices: It changes the control and operating boundary but still requires verified privacy, security, cost, and recovery
questions.explanation: Locality is a design fact, not proof of every desired property.

questions.prompt: What makes an ownership assignment operationally useful?
choices: Authority, evidence, escalation, on-call expectation, and a substitute
questions.explanation: Ownership must connect responsibility to authority, evidence, availability, and escalation.

questions.prompt: What is the safest first deployment shape?
choices: The smallest reversible shape that safely proves the next claim
questions.explanation: A bounded reversible step produces decision evidence without unnecessary operational scope.

gaps that prevent production use. Then we

repair a constraint-first selector. The

the failure consequences, and the owner

before choosing the platform. A label such

not by itself prove privacy, cost
efficiency, performance, availability, or
recoverability.

output modalities, sensitivity,
concurrency, arrival pattern, context

experiment, a shared internal service, and
a production dependency. They may use the

same operating commitment. Next, record

endpoint is slow, unavailable, overloaded,

wrong, unsafe, or unable to process a
request? A retry response, a safe refusal,

intentional behavior. Silent loss and

an undocumented bypass are not. A
deployment shape is suitable only when the

team can operate both the normal path and
the failure path. Starting with a

hardware catalog reverses this reasoning.

service around a purchase before success,
safety, and recovery have been defined.

class, dated September 21, 2026. It is

a synthetic internal support assistant

objective, or RTO, is 60 minutes. The

recovery point objective, or RPO, is 15
minutes. Inputs are retained for 7 days

for approved evaluation and then deleted.

enter an approved human queue. When

overloaded, the service returns a
retryable response instead of dropping

work. Unsafe or unprocessable requests
stop safely and go to human review. These

runtime, hardware, representative prompts,
and controlled load tests to establish

capacity and latency. This lab does not
execute a model and does not prove

that any service objective has been
achieved.

thermal limits may appear, and the machine

availability, or resource limits.

capacity, patching, power, cooling, spare

parts, physical access, and incidents.

constraining power, memory, update

bandwidth, physical security, and repair.

runtime name does not establish an

equivalent interface, license, context
limit, quality level, or operating
contract.

ranking. The mandatory constraints are a

verified match to the required data
boundary, RTO no worse than 60 minutes,

RPO no worse than 15 minutes, and a
qualified owner for the bounded

evaluation. Unknown evidence is
incomplete. It is not sufficient evidence.

and latency fit, 25 points; scalability,

20; operability, 20; reversibility, 15;
cost predictability, 10; and workload fit,

10. The exact synthetic arithmetic is as
follows. Workstation scores 4 plus 2 plus

2 plus 5 plus 3 plus 2, which equals 18.

15 plus 10 plus 10 plus 14 plus 8 plus 7,
which equals 64.

17 plus 12 plus 8 plus 7,

plus 5 plus 10 plus 10 plus

10 plus 10, which equals 55. Cloud service

plus 15 plus 9 plus 5, which equals 92.

plus 14 plus 10 plus 8 plus 5, which

eligibility evidence is equally important.

missing owner, so it is ineligible.
